entries.appliesTo: licensees, registrants, certificate holders, and other individuals lawfully permitted to provide psychotherapy services in Colorado; § 6-1-1705.2 also binds any person marketing an AI system as psychotherapy

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 2, 12-245-224.5(4)(a)(I)(A) — 'THE CLIENT OR THE CLIENT'S LEGALLY AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE IS INFORMED IN ADVANCE IN WRITING OF THE FOLLOWING: (A) THAT AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM WILL BE USED'; also (6)(b) — 'SHALL PROVIDE TO THE CLIENT DURING THE INITIAL CLIENT CONTACT WRITTEN INFORMATION CONCERNING PROHIBITIONS SPECIFIED IN SUBSECTION (6)(a) OF THIS SECTION ON THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 2, 12-245-224.5(4)(a)(II) — 'THE CLIENT OR THE CLIENT'S LEGALLY AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE CONSENTS IN WRITING TO THE USE OF THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'
dutySources.human-review: § 2, 12-245-224.5(5)(b) — 'GENERATE THERAPEUTIC RECOMMENDATIONS OR TREATMENT PLANS WITHOUT REVIEW AND APPROVAL BY THE LICENSEE, REGISTRANT, CERTIFICATE HOLDER, OR OTHER INDIVIDUAL LAWFULLY PERMITTED TO PROVIDE PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES IN THE STATE'; also (2) — 'MAINTAINS RESPONSIBILITY FOR REVIEWING ANY OUTPUTS OF THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 2, 12-245-224.5(5)(a) — 'SHALL NOT ALLOW AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM TO ... INTERACT WITH CLIENTS IN ANY FORM OF THERAPEUTIC COMMUNICATION WITHOUT SYNCHRONOUS, REAL-TIME INTERACTION BETWEEN THE LICENSEE, REGISTRANT, CERTIFICATE HOLDER, OR OTHER INDIVIDUAL LAWFULLY PERMITTED TO PROVIDE PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES IN THE STATE, THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM, AND THE CLIENT'; (6)(a) — 'SHALL NOT USE AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM TO PROVIDE, DIRECT, GUIDE, OR ATTEMPT TO PROVIDE, DIRECT, OR GUIDE PSYCHOTHERAPY ... UNLESS THE USE COMPLIES WITH SUBSECTION (5) OF THIS SECTION'
sources.consentRequired: § 2, 12-245-224.5(4)(a)(II) — 'CONSENTS IN WRITING TO THE USE OF THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'
sources.scope: § 2, 12-245-224.5(6)(a) — 'PSYCHOTHERAPY, CLINICAL INTERVENTION, COUNSELING, DIAGNOSIS, TREATMENT PLANNING, OR ANY OTHER ACTIVITY THAT CONSTITUTES THE PRACTICE OF PSYCHOTHERAPY'
sources.enforcer: § 1, 12-245-224(1) — 'A person licensed, registered, or certified under this article 245 violates this article 245 if the person: ... (y) FAILS TO COMPLY WITH SECTION 12-245-224.5 CONCERNING THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS.'

flags: Section 3 adds 6-1-1705.2 (codified in the Colorado Consumer Protection Act article) binding any person: prohibits terms in 'THE ADVERTISING, INTERFACE, OR OUTPUTS OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM' that imply the output 'IS BEING PROVIDED BY, IS ENDORSED BY, OR IS EQUIVALENT TO SERVICES PROVIDED BY' a licensed individual, that represent 'THAT THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM PROVIDES PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES', or that represent user data as confidential comparably to 'THERAPIST-CLIENT CONFIDENTIALITY' — this text states no penalty or enforcement mechanism for that section and shifts developer/deployer defect liability to 'APPLICABLE CONSUMER PROTECTION LAW' (rule 4: no imports), so exposure reflects only the article 245 discipline route in section 1

aiTherapyRule coded 'supervised' because autonomous AI therapeutic communication is barred but permitted with synchronous real-time provider participation (§ 12-245-224.5(5)(a)) and provider review/approval of recommendations ((5)(b)) — not an outright ban

AI recording/transcription of sessions is separately conditioned (§ 12-245-224.5(4)): advance written notice of use and purpose; consent is one-time — required 'ONLY FOR THE INITIAL USE OF THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM ... AND NOT FOR EACH SUBSEQUENT THERAPEUTIC SESSION, UNLESS THE PURPOSE OR MANNER OF USE MATERIALLY CHANGES' ((4)(b)); refusal or revocation 'SHALL NOT BE USED AS A BASIS TO DENY PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES' ((4)(a)(III))
Administrative and supplementary support uses are expressly permitted if the provider 'MAINTAINS RESPONSIBILITY FOR REVIEWING ANY OUTPUTS' (§ 12-245-224.5(2))

Carve-outs: accredited educational/training programs ((7)), IRB-overseen research ((8)), wellness tools and FDA-authorized behavioral-health products that 'DO NOT DIAGNOSE OR TREAT MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS' and 'CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY DISCLOSE THAT THE TECHNOLOGY OR SERVICE IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR CLINICAL CARE' ((9)); parallel carve-outs in 6-1-1705.2(3)-(5)
